docs.title: Biography
docs.text:
• Conrad really has something. That right there is good conducting because they actually listen to the music. Denise Ham

Conrad is an emerging orchestral conductor, with experience across symphonic, string, and wind ensemble repertoire. Their conducting style focuses on clarity and minimal distraction to the players, in order to encourage confidence and a diplomatic musical direction.

They currently hold positions within various on-campus ensembles. Following a previous engagement as Guest Conductor with the String Society, they return as its Principal Conductor for the 2026–27 season, alongside Assistant Conductor of the Wind Orchestra. Coming engagements with these ensembles, as part of Royal Holloway’s International Concert Series, include repertoire such as Gershwin’s Rhapsody in Blue.

Previously, they served as Junior Assistant Conductor of the Royal Holloway Symphony Orchestra under Rebecca Miller, contributing through conducting in rehearsals and sectional work. They have also engaged in rehearsal observation and feedback within departmental performance projects, including concerto and soloist collaborations.

Their orchestral training began at the Junior Royal Birmingham Conservatoire (JRBC) under Margarita Mikhailovna, alongside instrumental studies in flute (Liz Wrighton) and violin (Sam Mason). They have additionally received mentorship from Jeff Snowdon and Monica Leiher. After completing their studies at JRBC, aged 16, to pursue university education, they have participated in competitive conducting programmes and masterclasses. As one of four participants in a masterclass with Prof. Colin Metters, they worked on Berlioz’s Symphonie fantastique as part of the Girton Conducting Course. Through working with orchestral repertoire — including Schubert’s Symphony No. 5, Brahms’ Academic Festival Overture, Bizet’s L’Arlésienne suites, and Stravinsky’s Octet — they received tuition in the Toscanini–Barzin technique under tutors including Dominic Grier, Cathal Garvey, Leif Tse, and Denise Ham, who remarked that “Conrad really has something. That right there is good conducting because they actually listen to the music.” They were also selected as one of four participants for the North London Symphony Orchestra masterclass, working on Brahms’ Symphony No. 2 with Robert Max.

Apart from their musical endeavours, Conrad is currently a 3rd year Theoretical Physics BSc student at Royal Holloway, where their academic background motivated an analytical approach to score study.

docs.title: Physics
docs.text: Curious-minded and dedicated 3rd year Theoretical Physics (BSc.) student at Royal Holloway with significant research experience gained through past and ongoing projects. Aspiring to pursue a career in Mathematical Physics, particularly in Quantum Foundations.

docs.title: Testing quantum gravity
docs.text: Unifying General Relativity and Quantum Theory is one of the open problems of Physics. In recent years, some — such as the so-called BMV test — have proposed tests of Quantum Gravity which would enable a first experimental verification of whether a quantum theory of gravity should exist.

docs.title: Collapse models
docs.text: Another open problem in the field of Quantum Foundations is that of the Measurement Problem. Motivated by this, one possible "way out" is that of Collapse Models.

docs.title: Where the two meet
docs.text: Inspired by Roger Penrose's idea of gravity-induced collapse, I am also interested in the intersection of testing quantum gravity and collapse models, where one may benefit from — or interfere with — the other.

docs.title: SEPnet Competitive Funded Summer Research Programme — CQER-IQ
docs.text:
Jun 2026 – Aug 2026. Project co-supervisors: Dr. Richard Howl, Prof. Sougato Bose, Dr. Sravan Kumar.

  • Investigated entanglement measures in realistic scenario for an experimental proposal utilising Bose-Einstein Condensates, and their robustness under realistic noise models in support of ongoing research into tests of Quantum and Modified Gravity.
  • Derived analytical solutions of entanglement witnesses and mathematical proofs.
  • Implemented numerical simulations utilising Lindblad Master Equations, Stochastic Differential Equations, and Monte Carlo methods.

docs.title: Ongoing Research Projects — Royal Holloway
docs.text:
2025–present. Independent research, continued from previous summer projects.

  • Developed Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) approaches for solving nonlinear PDEs and created computational notebooks and a Python package for the Schrödinger-Newton equation ( Learning-PINN).
  • Investigated tensions between tests of quantum gravity and gravitationally-induced collapse models, and analysed their mutual implications.

docs.title: Casimir Effect in Tabletop Experiment for Quantum Gravity
docs.text:
Royal Holloway, Aug 2025. Project supervisor: Dr. Richard Howl.

  • Investigated the effects of gravitational redshift on the Casimir contribution in the Bose–Marletto–Vedral experiment.
  • Performed von Neumann entropy calculations and computational simulations using Wolfram Mathematica ( Gravity-Entropy).
